overall_summary: Deduplicated performance analysis reveals that 'What If' hypothetical space scenarios and extreme planetary anomalies (such as liquid diamond worlds, extreme dark exoplanets, and extreme time/physics quirks) generate the highest view velocity, likes-per-view, and sustained engagement compared to standard biological facts or historical mysteries.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (YlDuGu1vzAg) achieved over 800-1,000+ views rapidly with exceptionally high like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on cinematic hypothetical space physics scenarios ('What if you fell into...') using high-contrast visual hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing impossible physical environments like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) outperform generic space facts.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing short-form deep dives into bizarre, visually striking exoplanets with extreme atmospheric conditions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics covering basic animal stats (e.g., octopus hearts) or generic psychological tricks received lower view counts and zero engagement compared to space anomalies.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard animal/brain facts unless framed through a high-stakes survival or extreme-anomaly lens.
